summary: Repair Astra CORRECT findings: compare canonical typed lesson serialization and classify seed-, evaluation-context-, and policy-bound idea identity before candidate execution.
implementation: NegativeKnowledge.save writes a schema-versioned canonical JSON payload with SHA-256 integrity; create mode prevents replacing an existing snapshot.
NegativeKnowledge.load validates envelope, version, content hash, lesson shape, and unique lesson IDs before exposing a fresh store.

Rejected lesson mappings are detached on storage and when read. Full lesson comparison uses canonical JSON SHA-256, distinguishing values such as true and 1. Reusing an ID with changed serialized content returns CONFLICT and preserves the original lesson.

Optimizer preflight uses a stable idea identity over lesson ID, hypothesis, cohort, affected policy, proposed change, risks, and a fingerprint of policy module source, bytecode, and captured configuration. It runs before candidate evaluation, robustness, CandidatePolicy, and tournament work.

Preflight binds the seed, scenario registry, optimizer/evaluator/robustness/tournament source modules, and policy identity. Missing source fingerprints or changed run context produce top-level CONFLICT rather than reuse.

Preflight reports REJECTED_IDEA with the stored full lesson digest; it does not label preflight identity as whole-record equality. Changed idea, policy, seed, or evaluation context returns top-level CONFLICT, while other candidates proceed.

The optimizer reuse test saves the rejected lesson, loads it into a fresh NegativeKnowledge instance, and verifies the same-context second run skips it before candidate evaluation, robustness, CandidatePolicy, and tournament. Tests cover bool/int identity distinction, changed seed/source-context conflict, and mismatched snapshot schema.
Default optimizer behavior and holdout promotion gates remain unchanged; no real-world accuracy claim is made.
